samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the picture graph. How many apples were counted?
Look at the picture graph. How many books were read on Thursday?
Look at the picture graph. What is the difference between cats and dogs?
Look at the picture graph. What is the total number of flowers shown?
Look at the picture graph. How many sunflowers are in the garden?
Look at the picture graph. What is the difference between Grade 1 and Grade 4?
Look at the picture graph. What is the total number of sports shown?
Look at the picture graph. What is the total number of colors shown?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Reading single rows and computing differences is squarely interpretive, but two stems ask for the total number of sports shown and the total number of colors shown while the keys (13 and 10) are sums of the tallies, not counts of the categories named. A pupil who answers the question as literally worded - how many sports - is marked wrong.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Three interpretive moves appear (read one row, compare two rows, total all rows) but the most basic pictograph question of all is missing: no sample asks which category has the most or the fewest, and none asks a yes/no comparison. That omission leaves the easiest and most common interpretation demand unsampled.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Counting symbols, taking a difference of at most 4, and summing four small rows to a total under 16 are within reach at Quarter 3 of Grade 1, and each stem is a single short question after Look at the picture graph.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Although every item is a four-option read question - correct, since the graph must be on screen - the underlying task genuinely rotates among row-reading, difference-finding and totalling, and the subject matter moves across fruit, books by day, animals, flowers, grade levels, sports and colours.

competency_alignment.rationale: The progression from reading one row, to comparing two, to summing the whole graph is a real ladder of interpretation difficulty built on this competency rather than on arithmetic dressing.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Row values stay small enough to count symbol by symbol and the largest total shown is 15, which keeps the summing items inside Grade 1 addition even though the competency itself states no ceiling.
